items.q: A 62-year-old man has extensive deep vein thrombosis with active gastrointestinal bleeding that forbids all anticoagulation. His haemoglobin falls daily. Which absolute indication best earns an IVC filter in this bleeding clot patient?
o: Mild calf ache without any clot
Bleeding that welcomes more blood thinners
No clot with prophylactic wishes only
items.exp:
**Answer: A - Venous thromboembolism with anticoagulation contraindicated.** Proven clots with bleeding that forbids drugs leave filters as the only pulmonary shield.
**Why the others are wrong**
- B: Aches without clots earn nothing
- C: Bleeding forbids thinners directly
- D: Wishes never justify filters
**Key point:** Bleeding clots earn filters.
items.kp: Clots with contraindicated drugs earn IVC filters.

items.q: A 45-year-old woman has a massive iliofemoral clot burden with borderline reserve after brain surgery last week. Drugs are temporarily impossible. Which device-duration logic best suits this temporarily undruggable massive clot?
o: Retrievable filter with retrieval planned from day one
items.exp:
**Answer: A - Retrievable filter with retrieval planned from day one.** Temporary contraindications resolve where planned retrieval prevents forgotten permanence.
**Why the others are wrong**
- B: Permanent overshoots temporary blocks
- C: Fingers never filter emboli
- D: Ligation overshoots hugely
**Key point:** Temporary blocks take retrievable filters.
items.kp: Temporary contraindications suit retrievable filters.

items.q: A 58-year-old man has his retrievable filter in place for eight months with progressive tilt on surveillance. Anticoagulation resumed long ago. Which dwell-time logic best retrieves this tilted long-dwelling filter now?
o: Embedment and perforation rise with months so retrieve promptly
items.exp:
**Answer: A - Embedment and perforation rise with months so retrieve promptly.** Apices scar into walls over months where delayed snares tear cavae, so resumed drugs trigger retrieval.
**Why the others are wrong**
- B: Dwell scars filters in
- C: Tilt worsens with waiting
- D: Resumed drugs invite retrieval
**Key point:** Long dwell with resumed drugs retrieves.
items.kp: Long-dwelling filters with resumed drugs come out.

items.q: A 50-year-old woman has her filter snared through jugular access after clots cleared and drugs resumed. Cavagram shows a clean cava. Which retrieval-condition logic best confirms readiness with cleared traps and resumed drugs?
o: Empty filters with anticoagulation aboard retrieve safely
items.exp:
**Answer: A - Empty filters with anticoagulation aboard retrieve safely.** Cleared traps release no emboli where resumed drugs guard the retrieval itself.
**Why the others are wrong**
- B: Full traps embolise on pull
- C: Drugs guard retrievals
- D: Cavagrams map traps
**Key point:** Cleared traps with drugs retrieve.
items.kp: Empty filters with resumed drugs retrieve safely.

items.q: A 66-year-old man develops sudden chest pain with arrhythmia two weeks after filter placement. Imaging shows the filter in his right atrium. Which migration logic best rescues this atrial filter migrant urgently?
o: Snare rescue retrieving the migrated device at once
items.exp:
**Answer: A - Snare rescue retrieving the migrated device at once.** Cardiac metal perforates and embolises further where snares reclaim it before catastrophe.
**Why the others are wrong**
- B: Watched metal perforates
- C: Pain warns of migration
- D: Arrhythmias demand retrieval
**Key point:** Migrated filters snare urgently.
items.kp: Atrial filter migration needs urgent snare rescue.

items.q: A 55-year-old woman has back pain with a tilted filter strut perforating her caval wall on CT. She stays haemodynamically stable. Which perforation logic best assesses stable strut perforation urgently without panic?
o: Urgent assessment since stable perforations still threaten organs
items.exp:
**Answer: A - Urgent assessment since stable perforations still threaten organs.** Struts near duodenum and aorta injure neighbours where planning prevents catastrophe.
**Why the others are wrong**
- B: Stable still threatens
- C: Pain warns of struts
- D: Ignored struts injure
**Key point:** Stable perforations assess urgently.
items.kp: Stable strut perforation needs urgent assessment.

items.q: A 70-year-old man develops bilateral leg swelling with prominent abdominal wall collaterals three months after filter placement. Duplex shows caval thrombosis. Which caval-thrombosis logic best explains bilateral swelling with collaterals?
o: Blocked cavae reroute blood through skin veins
items.exp:
**Answer: A - Blocked cavae reroute blood through skin veins.** Thrombosed filters dam caval flow where abdominal collaterals carry blood visibly.
**Why the others are wrong**
- B: Bilateral means central block
- C: Collaterals mark obstruction
- D: Filters invite clots
**Key point:** Bilateral swelling with collaterals means caval thrombosis.
items.kp: Bilateral swelling with collaterals means IVC thrombosis.

items.q: A 48-year-old woman has no clot but requests a prophylactic filter before high-risk surgery. The team debates justification. Which prophylaxis logic best restrains filters without proven clots?
o: Unproven clots need documented justification since filters harm too
items.exp:
**Answer: A - Unproven clots need documented justification since filters harm too.** Prophylactic metal migrates and clots where benefit stays theoretical without thrombus.
**Why the others are wrong**
- B: Wishes never justify metal
- C: Filters harm truly
- D: Surgery rarely needs filters
**Key point:** Prophylactic filters need justification.
items.kp: Prophylactic filters need documented justification.

items.q: A 63-year-old man has residual clot trapped in his filter on pre-retrieval cavagram. His legs look better but the trap stays full. Which trapped-clot logic best postpones retrieval until anticoagulation clears filters?
o: Pulling full traps embolises lungs directly
items.exp:
**Answer: A - Pulling full traps embolises lungs directly.** Snared filters release their catch downstream where waiting with drugs empties traps first.
**Why the others are wrong**
- B: Full traps shower lungs
- C: Traps embolise readily
- D: Cavagrams map traps
**Key point:** Full traps wait for clearance.
items.kp: Clot-filled filters wait for anticoagulant clearance.

items.q: A 52-year-old woman has lifelong antiphospholipid syndrome with recurrent clots despite newer agents. Her contraindication looks permanent. Which permanence logic best suits lifelong blocks to permanent devices?
items.exp:
**Answer: A - Lifelong contraindications earn permanent filters.** Never-resolving blocks need lasting shields where retrieval planning wastes effort.
**Why the others are wrong**
- B: Permanent matches lifelong
- C: Lifelong still clots
- D: Devices shield rather than cure
**Key point:** Lifelong blocks take permanent filters.
items.kp: Lifelong contraindications suit permanent filters.

items.q: A 59-year-old man has a filter placed at a referring hospital with no follow-up arranged. Six months later nobody knows its type. Which clinic logic best tracks every filter so none become forgotten permanence?
o: Filter clinics register every device with retrieval dates
items.exp:
**Answer: A - Filter clinics register every device with retrieval dates.** Tracked filters retrieve on schedule where lost ones embed and perforate silently.
**Why the others are wrong**
- B: Clinics prevent forgetting
- C: Unknown filters embed
- D: Follow-up retrieves
**Key point:** Filter clinics track every device.
items.kp: Filter clinics register every device with dates.

items.q: A 44-year-old woman has her tilted filter freed with forceps after snares failed. The apex had scarred into the wall. Which advanced-retrieval logic best frees embedded apices where snares slip?
o: Forceps grasp scarred apices that loops cannot hook
items.exp:
**Answer: A - Forceps grasp scarred apices that loops cannot hook.** Endobronchial-style forceps bite tissue-capped hooks where slippery loops slide off.
**Why the others are wrong**
- B: Snares slip off scars
- C: Embedded often free
- D: Forceps suit cavae
**Key point:** Embedded apices need forceps.
items.kp: Embedded filter apices need forceps retrieval.

items.q: A 67-year-old man restarts anticoagulation the day after filter placement for his proven clots. The team explains filters never dissolve clots. Which adjunct logic best pairs resumed drugs with fresh filters?
o: Filters shield lungs while drugs dissolve leg clots
items.exp:
**Answer: A - Filters shield lungs while drugs dissolve leg clots.** Metal catches strays where anticoagulation clears the source thrombus itself.
**Why the others are wrong**
- B: Filters catch rather than dissolve
- C: Drugs clear sources
- D: Legs need clearing
**Key point:** Fresh filters pair with resumed drugs.
items.kp: Fresh filters need resumed anticoagulation.

items.q: A 50-year-old man has perioperative high-risk orthopaedic surgery with prior clots and temporary drug stops. A retrievable filter covers the window. Which window logic best times perioperative filters around drug stops?
o: Bridge drug-free windows with temporary shields
items.exp:
**Answer: A - Bridge drug-free windows with temporary shields.** Operative drug pauses expose clotters where retrievable shields cover the gap.
**Why the others are wrong**
- B: Windows expose clotters
- C: Temporary matches brief
- D: Surgery allows filters
**Key point:** Perioperative windows bridge with filters.
items.kp: Perioperative drug windows bridge with retrievable filters.

items.q: A 56-year-old woman has her filter clinic letter filed with retrieval booked at six weeks. Her anticoagulation restarts next week. Which planning logic best books retrieval dates from the day of placement?
items.exp:
**Answer: A - Day-one planning prevents forgotten permanence.** Booked dates trigger recall where unbooked filters embed silently for years.
**Why the others are wrong**
- B: Planning prevents forgetting
- C: Dates drive recall
- D: Filters never self-retrieve
**Key point:** Retrieval dates book at placement.
items.kp: Filter retrieval dates book on placement day.

items.q: A 61-year-old man has massive clot burden with poor reserve and a temporary drug block from head injury. The MDT picks a retrievable filter. Which burden logic best matches massive burdens with poor reserve to temporary shields?
o: Big clots with fragile patients merit shields till drugs resume
items.exp:
**Answer: A - Big clots with fragile patients merit shields till drugs resume.** Large thrombus with nowhere to tolerate emboli needs bridging where heads heal.
**Why the others are wrong**
- B: Massive clots shower readily
- C: Fragile need shields most
- D: Heads heal with time
**Key point:** Massive burdens bridge till drugs.
items.kp: Massive clots with poor reserve bridge with filters.

items.q: A 47-year-old woman asks whether her filter treats her leg clots directly. The nurse explains shields versus treatment clearly. Which education logic best separates lung shielding from clot treatment?
o: Filters catch strays while drugs and legs heal themselves
items.exp:
**Answer: A - Filters catch strays while drugs and legs heal themselves.** Metal guards lungs where anticoagulation with compression clears legs.
**Why the others are wrong**
- B: Filters guard rather than dissolve
- C: Education guides expectations
- D: Legs need drugs
**Key point:** Filters shield lungs, drugs treat legs.
items.kp: Filters shield lungs while drugs treat leg clots.

items.q: A 68-year-old man has laser sheath retrieval of a five-year embedded filter with dense scarring. The procedure succeeds without caval tear. Which laser logic best cuts through scar where force fails?
items.exp:
**Answer: A - Photoablation vaporises scar gripping apices.** Excimer energy sublimates fibrous caps where traction alone tears cavae.
**Why the others are wrong**
- B: Lasers cut scar precisely
- C: Scar grips apices firmly
- D: Old often free with lasers
**Key point:** Laser sheaths free scarred filters.
items.kp: Long-embedded filters may need laser sheath retrieval.

items.q: A 54-year-old woman has her caval injury mapped after difficult retrieval with a small contained leak. The team watches with repeat imaging. Which contained-leak logic best watches small caval leaks without blushes?
o: Tamponaded retroperitoneum heals small contained caval leaks
items.exp:
**Answer: A - Tamponaded retroperitoneum heals small contained caval leaks.** Contained low-pressure venous leaks seal where scans confirm resolution.
**Why the others are wrong**
- B: Surgery suits free bleeds
- C: Scans confirm sealing
- D: Small leaks seal
**Key point:** Small contained caval leaks watch.
items.kp: Small contained caval leaks watch with repeat imaging.

items.q: A 60-year-old man completes filter retrieval with a clean post cavagram and patent cava. His drugs continue with clinic follow-up. Which completion logic best confirms clean cavae with continued drugs after retrieval?
o: Clean cavagrams with drugs aboard close retrieval episodes
Drugs stop the moment filters leave
items.exp:
**Answer: A - Clean cavagrams with drugs aboard close retrieval episodes.** Patent cavae with ongoing source treatment prove the episode resolved safely.
**Why the others are wrong**
- B: Follow-up continues regardless
- C: Drugs continue for sources
- D: Cavagrams prove patency
**Key point:** Clean cavagrams close retrievals.
items.kp: Clean post-retrieval cavagrams with drugs close episodes.

items.q: A 57-year-old woman has suprarenal filter placement due to a low-lying clot reaching her renal veins. The operator positions above the renal mouths. Which suprarenal logic best places filters above renal veins when clots climb high?
o: High clots need shields above their top extent
items.exp:
**Answer: A - High clots need shields above their top extent.** Filters guard downstream lungs only when stationed above the highest thrombus.
**Why the others are wrong**
- B: Suprarenal spares kidneys carefully
- C: Low clots take infrarenal shields
- D: Renals govern placement height
**Key point:** High clots take suprarenal shields.
items.kp: High-climbing clots need suprarenal filters.

items.q: A 63-year-old man has duplicated IVC discovered on cavagram with clots in both channels. The team places bilateral filters. Which duplication logic best explains bilateral shields in duplicated cavae?
o: Twin channels both carry emboli to lungs
items.exp:
**Answer: A - Twin channels both carry emboli to lungs.** Each caval limb bypasses single filters where bilateral shields guard both streams.
**Why the others are wrong**
- B: Duplications carry clots truly
- C: Singles miss second channels
- D: Duplications exist rarely
**Key point:** Duplicated cavae take bilateral filters.
items.kp: Duplicated IVC needs bilateral filters.

items.q: A 49-year-old woman has her filter strut abutting her duodenum without penetration on CT. The team retrieves electively with surgical backup. Which abutment logic best retrieves electively before penetration completes?
o: Near-miss struts retrieve before boring through
items.exp:
**Answer: A - Near-miss struts retrieve before boring through.** Abutting metal erodes slowly where elective retrieval with backup prevents fistulae.
**Why the others are wrong**
- B: Abutments progress to fistulae
- C: Duodenums perforate badly
- D: Backup rescues trouble
**Key point:** Abutting struts retrieve electively.
items.kp: Duodenal-abutting struts retrieve electively with backup.

items.q: A 71-year-old man with limited life expectancy and permanent drug contraindication receives a permanent filter without clinic enrolment. Which limited-expectancy logic best matches permanent devices to palliative contexts?
o: Lasting shields without retrieval burden suit limited horizons
items.exp:
**Answer: A - Lasting shields without retrieval burden suit limited horizons.** Permanent metal guards remaining months where retrieval appointments burden dying patients.
**Why the others are wrong**
- B: Retrieval burdens palliation
- C: Expectancy guides choice
- D: Some cases skip clinics
**Key point:** Palliative blocks take permanent shields.
items.kp: Palliative permanent blocks suit permanent filters.

items.q: A 55-year-old woman has her filter decision documented with indication, device type and retrieval date in the notes. The night team follows the plan seamlessly. Which documentation logic best records filters for seamless team care?
o: Complete filter notes let every team track and retrieve
items.exp:
**Answer: A - Complete filter notes let every team track and retrieve.** Indication with device and dates tells all teams what to watch and when to pull.
**Why the others are wrong**
- B: Notes guide night care
- C: Guessing loses filters
- D: Documentation saves time
**Key point:** Filter notes direct team tracking.
items.kp: Complete filter documentation directs team tracking.
